REGISTERED ESTABLISHMENT
EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for apples (horticulture). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-WA-2021-0199 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 17 August 2021 and the current registration period extends to 16 August 2024. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Rosa Tavares is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2015. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered premises comprise Lot 41 on Plan DP 530406, located at 56 South Western Highway, Manjimup WA 6258. The total registered area is 22.5 hectares. The registered boundary is delineated on the attached site plan (Appendix A) and includes all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure. Adjoining land parcels and access roads are excluded from the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites

The registered premises adjoin: (north) sealed public road; (east) cropping paddocks under same ownership; (south) state forest reserve — no stock or chemical activities; (west) neighbour's mixed-farming property — grain growing, no spray operations within 200 m.
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: apples is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of apples. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

An extension to the existing cold storage facility was completed in February 2025, increasing capacity from 120 to 280 pallets. The extension involved modification of the existing coolroom envelope and installation of additional refrigeration plant. DAFF was not notified prior to commencement of works.

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

4. Hazard Analysis
5. HACCP Control Chart — Monitoring and Corrective Action
6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

Hygiene and Sanitation Program (NQGT-HSP-001):
• Terminal cleaning: receival pit cleaned weekly; conveyor gallery swept daily; elevator boots washed monthly.
• Between commodities: blow-down of all conveyors and elevator legs before changing grain type.
• Vessel loading spout cleaned after each vessel loading.
• Personnel: safety footwear and dust masks required in operational areas; handwash on entry.
• Records: Cleaning Register (NQGT-CLN-01).

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
Waste management procedures for Spencer Gulf Fisheries & Grain Pty Ltd are NOT included in this HACCP plan. No waste streams, disposal methods, frequencies or records are documented.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

Pest Control Program (NQGT-PCP-001):
• 12 internal bait stations (Bromadiolone) in terminal building.
• Insect pitfall traps in 4 export silos.
• Phosphine fumigation available on request.
⚠ DEFICIENCY: No monitoring schedule specifying inspection frequency. No corrective action procedure if rodent activity or insect infestation is detected. Pest effectiveness CANNOT be demonstrated without documented monitoring records and corrective actions. See CCP-4 above.
ACTION: Add monitoring schedule (fortnightly inspections) and corrective action procedure.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

Traceability System (NQGT-TRACE-001):
• Receival dockets: grower → truck rego → weight → silo allocation.
• Silo inventory log: daily balance per silo.
• Vessel loading manifest: lists source silos, quantities, blending ratios, fumigation certificate ref.
• Retained 2 years.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.

Failed Goods Procedure (NQGT-FGP-001):
• Mycotoxin/MRL failure: silo on HOLD; NATA retest; if confirmed — downgrade to domestic feed.
• Vessel rejection: grain returned to terminal silo; re-inspect; document; DAFF notified.
• Records: Non-Conformance Register (NQGT-NCR-01).
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

Phytosanitary Security (NQGT-PSP-001):
• Vessel hold surveyed and approved by DAFF before loading.
• Phytosanitary certificate issued per vessel by DAFF.
• Post-fumigation grain not moved until DAFF sampling complete.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Manjimup Horticulture Exports is a registered export establishment located at 56 South Western Highway, Manjimup WA 6258, WA. The establishment holds RE Number RE-WA-2021-0199 and is registered to handle and export Berries under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERWAES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Berries.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

LED high-bay luminaires throughout: 450 lux processing, 360 lux storage, 342 lux load-out. All levels comply with AS/NZS 1680.2.1. Photocell-activated perimeter lighting for after-hours vehicle movements.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Amenities block adjacent to processing entry: 1 toilet, 1 hand basin (hot/cold, liquid soap, paper towels). Additional hand basin at packing hall entry — no-touch sensor tap, soap, paper towel roll. 'Wash hands before handling product' signage at all wash points.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Internal surfaces: smooth-finish epoxy-sealed concrete floors with 80 mm coved skirting; smooth food-grade colourbond wall linings to 2.4 m; recessed drains with stainless-steel grates. All equipment on adjustable SS feet ≥150 mm off floor. Equipment housings open fully for pressure-wash access. Cleaning schedule specifies full washdown between commodity lots.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Sealed building envelope: all wall-floor junctions coved; roof-wall junctions sealed with foam backer rod and polyurethane sealant; all service penetrations sealed with expandable foam; ventilation openings fitted with 6 mm stainless wire mesh; personnel doors with 10 mm brush seals on all four sides; roller doors with rubber threshold sweeps and side brush seals. Annual pest technician inspection confirms envelope integrity.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Liquid waste via flush-recessed floor drains to bunded underground sump (1500 L) outside the building; pump-out by licensed contractor weekly or when 80% full. Solid waste in sealed labelled bins at designated collection points; removed to covered external waste bay daily. Dust via cyclone separator — collection bags changed fortnightly. All waste areas bunded and roofed.
6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Documented Waste Management Procedure (WMP-1601 Rev 2): specifies daily spillage sweep, weekly sump pump-out, post-commodity full shed washdown. Responsibilities assigned to named positions. Records in waste management log (Form WL-001) retained ≥2 years. Procedure reviewed annually by establishment manager.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

The floor drain channels in the processing area contain organic residue carried over from the previous season's operations — the end-of-season drain flush was not completed. Residue volume estimated at 15–25 kg of decomposing berries material and washdown solids. Flies have been attracted to the drain area. Drain channels are scheduled for cleanout prior to next season's receival.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

No pest activity detected at most recent internal inspection. All rodent bait stations serviceable and baited — no evidence of feeding. Insect monitoring traps (pheromone and sticky) show no target species above threshold levels. No evidence of bird ingress. Last fumigation: 2024 (routine, bin rotation).

1. ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment

This plan covers all areas of Manjimup Horticulture Exports used in pulse cleaning, storage and packing operations for export Lentils. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Lentils during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival / Intake Hopper

After each intake run: Lock out receiving conveyor. Use compressed air lance to dislodge pulse residue from hopper walls, conveyor trough, and all transition points. Vacuum accumulated screenings and fine material. Inspect underside of conveyor belt for product trapping. Record in Intake Checklist.
Cleaner / Aspirator / Colour Sorter

After each cleaning run: Remove accumulated screenings from collection trays and hoppers. Brush aspirator screens with dedicated brush to remove lodged seeds. For colour sorter: follow manufacturer's lens cleaning protocol. Vacuum sensor housings. Inspect all filters and replace if blocked. Record in Plant Operator Run Log.
Storage Silos / Bins

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Storage Silos / Bins in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
Packing Line / Bagging Machine

End of each shift: Clear all pulse product from the line. Vacuum or brush conveyor belts, weigh hoppers, and bag former guides to remove pulse fines. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe external surfaces of bagging machine and packing bench. Check sealing jaws and heat elements for residue. Record in Shift Log.
Palletising Area / Loading Dock

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Palletising Area / Loading Dock in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Dead-stock accumulation occurs in aspirator collection trays, conveyor trough joints, and under the bagging machine floor plate. These areas are vacuumed or blown out at each run change to prevent insect harbourage.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System

Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES

Each area supervisor completes a sign-off on the shift cleaning record, confirming that cleaning has been carried out to the required standard. The site manager reviews all records at the end of each production day.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

Where a cleaning deficiency is identified, the affected area is immediately re-cleaned before any product handling recommences. The deficiency, cause, and corrective action taken are recorded in the Non-Conformance Register. Repeat occurrences trigger a review of the relevant SOP.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

At the most recent internal inspection (4 February 2025), all areas of Manjimup Horticulture Exports were found to be in a clean and hygienic condition consistent with the requirements of this plan. No deficiencies were identified.
